Natural fibre-reinforced polymer composites are increasingly investigated as sustainable alternatives to synthetic fibre composites because of their low density, renewability, and reduced environmental impact. Here, continuous flax fibre/epoxy laminates with unidirectional (UD), bidirectional (BD), angle-ply, and quasi-isotropic configurations were fabricated using vacuum-assisted resin transfer moulding. Their structural, thermal, viscoelastic, and fatigue properties were evaluated for lightweight applications.

X-ray diffraction showed approximately 23% crystallinity across all configurations. Thermogravimetric analysis revealed three-stage degradation, indicating stability below 200 °C. Dynamic mechanical analysis showed higher glass-transition temperature and storage modulus in reinforced laminates than in neat epoxy, with responses influenced by fibre orientation. Tensile and flexural tests demonstrated that UD laminates had the highest stiffness and strength, while BD laminates offered greater strain-carrying ability and multidirectional performance.

Tension–tension fatigue tests at stress ratios of 0.1 and 0.2 and stress levels of 50–80% of ultimate tensile strength showed better fatigue performance in UD laminates. Stiffness degradation followed three stages: initial fibre–matrix interactions, progressive matrix cracking and delamination, and final fibre breakage. FESEM identified fibre pull-out, matrix cracking, fibre–matrix debonding, and fatigue striations. Overall, the findings demonstrate that laminate architecture influences flax fibre/epoxy composite performance and support its potential for sustainable automotive, civil, and lightweight structural applications.
keywords: Composites; fatigue; Characterization; fracture

name: Phurailatpam Sujata Devi
discipline: School of Agro and Rural Technology
thesis_title: SEASONAL DYNAMICS OF INVERTEBRATE ABUNDANCE IN ORGANIC WASTE COMPOSTING AND OPTIMIZATION OF BLACK SOLDIER FLY LARVAE FOR WASTE BIOCONVERSION
abstract:
This study investigated seasonal invertebrate dynamics during pile composting and evaluated black soldier fly larvae (BSFL) for organic waste bioconversion. Invertebrate communities were surveyed in vegetable waste, water hyacinth and Mikania micrantha composting systems across summer, monsoon and winter. Springtails dominated, followed by mites and BSFL, while community abundance and diversity varied with substrate and season and were associated with physicochemical parameters.

BSFL performance was assessed on vegetable waste (T0), vegetable waste–sawdust (6.5:0.5; T1) and vegetable waste–cow dung–sawdust (5:4:1; T2). T0 achieved the greatest waste reduction (94.10%), T2 shortened processing to 11 days and supported the highest survival, and T1 yielded the highest crude protein content (45.5%). Evaluation of eight formulations identified VW:CD:SD at 6:3:1 (R2) as the best treatment, achieving 74.69% waste reduction and 96.39% larval survival. Metagenomic profiling of R2-reared larvae revealed a gut microbial community with functional potential in carbohydrate and amino acid metabolism. Finally, mixed cooked and vegetable waste was assessed: the 3:1 formulation (S5) achieved 65.15% waste reduction and 90.2% survival, produced prepupae with the highest crude protein content (40.04%). Collectively, these findings connect compost-associated invertebrate ecology with BSFL bioconversion, supporting integrated organic waste treatment and recovery of protein-rich biomass and nutrient-rich frass.
keywords: Black Soldier Fly larvae; invertebrates; Mikania micrantha; millipedes; mites; springtails; vegetable waste; Water hyacinth

name: PIKESH KUMAR
thesis_title: Sustainable Production of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural from Biomass through Catalytic Hydrothermal Liquefaction
abstract: The development of sustainable catalytic pathways for converting lignocellulosic biomass into value-added platform chemicals and renewable energy products is essential for advancing a bio-based economy. This study investigates the thermochemical conversion and catalytic valorization of lignocellulosic biomass, with particular emphasis on 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF) production through hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL). Melocanna baccifera and Royal Poinciana were investigated as potential feedstocks, while pyrolysis and co-pyrolysis were employed to explore their conversion behaviour and the production of biochar and bio-oil as potential alternatives to petroleum-derived products. The resulting biochar was further engineered through metal incorporation and acid functionalization to develop heterogeneous catalysts with tailored surface properties and acid-site characteristics. The roles of Brønsted and Lewis acid sites in promoting carbohydrate hydrolysis, dehydration, and furanic compound formation were systematically investigated. The influence of catalyst composition, reaction temperature, solvent environment, and operating parameters on conversion behaviour and product distribution was evaluated. Furthermore, catalyst regeneration and reusability were examined to assess catalytic stability, while life cycle assessment (LCA) was conducted to evaluate the environmental impacts and process sustainability. Overall, this study integrates biomass conversion, catalyst engineering, and environmental assessment towards sustainable biorefinery development.
keywords: Hydrothermal Liquefaction; Pyrolysis; Life Cycle Assessment;5-HMF;

name: Pooja Kumari
thesis_title: Studies of Structural, Optical and Electrical properties of Titanium and Molybdenum doped ITO thin films deposited using Pulsed laser deposition
abstract: Transparent conducting oxides are key materials for modern optoelectronics and photonics devices. Indium tin oxide (ITO) is widely used industry standard material. The high cost and scarcity of indium limit its wider use. Transition metal doping, Titanium and molybdenum are promising dopants for modifying the optoelectronic properties of ITO. Pulsed laser deposition was chosen for its near-stoichiometric transfer of target composition to film, energetic plasma-assisted growth and control of deposition conditions. In the Ti-doped films, the optoelectronic properties improvement indicates that a thinner or lower-cost film can deliver equivalent device performance, with direct implications for material consumption and manufacturing economics. Equally important is the shift in plasma crossover wavelength, since the plasma wavelength determines where the material transitions from dielectric to metallic behaviour. The molybdenum incorporation shows the structural, photoluminescence and electrical response evolve with growth of deposition conditions. Beyond linear behaviour, the films show promise in the nonlinear optical regime. Degenerately doped oxides with tunable plasma wavelengths are strong candidates for optical switching and optical limiting, functions that are central to ultrafast photonic circuits and laser-safety components. The doping strategy which improves the transparent-electrode performance also enhances nonlinear response, which is an advantage in integrated photonic platforms.
keywords: Laser; Plasmonics; Nonlinear optics; Nanomaterials; Material science; Optical characterization; Optoelectronics; Numerical modeling; Thin film characterization; Optical sensing

name: PRAGATISHEEL
thesis_title: Production of butanol, a drop-in fuel biofuel from molasses via Clostridium sp.
abstract: Growing demand of sustainable fuels has intensified interest in biobutanol as a renewable alternative to petroleum derived fuels. This thesis develops an economically viable, intensified acetone-butanol-ethanol (ABE) fermentation process using sugarcane molasses and Clostridium saccharobutylicum. Molasses was characterized to access its suitability as a low-cost feedstock. Fermentation medium components were screened and optimized using Response surface methodology and Artificial Neural Network-Genetic Algorithm modelling, followed by experimental validation. Batch and fed-batch fermentations were investigated to improve substrate utilization and solvent production while addressing substrate inhibition and butanol toxicity. Kinetic modelling was conducted to describe fermentation dynamics and quantify relationships among substrate consumption, biomass growth and product formation. To mitigate product inhibition, an integrated in situ recovery strategy combining gas stripping and adsorption onto AmberSep® Optipore® L-493 resin was developed. Resin Adsorption, desorption and regeneration characteristics were evaluated to assess its reusability. Integrating product recovery with fermentation increased butanol productivity from 0.20 to 0.30 g/L/h compared with batch fermentation without recovery. Overall, this work demonstrates the potential of combining feedstock characterization, medium optimization, controlled feeding, kinetic analysis and in situ product recovery to advance molasses-based biobutanol production and improve the economic feasibility and operational performance of ABE fermentation for process intensification.
keywords: Biofuels; Butanol; Acetone-Butanol-Ethanol (ABE) Fermentation; Media Optimization; Design-Expert; Response Surface Methodology; Artificial Neural Network-Genetic Optimization; Product Recovery; Gas stripping; Adsorption; Adsorption Isotherm; Liquid-gas adsorption; Batch Fermentation; Fed-Batch Fermentation; Bioreactor; Kinetic Modelling

name: Pratham Singh
thesis_title: Lagrangian Coherent Structure Analysis of Unsteady Heat Transfer in Vortex-Shedding Flows Past Bluff Bodies Using High-Order Compact Schemes
abstract:
My research builds computational tools to understand and predict unsteady heat transfer in flow past bluff bodies, including heated circular and inclined elliptical cylinders. It combines computational fluid dynamics (CFD), mathematical modelling and Lagrangian particle tracking to show how fluid motion and coherent flow structures govern thermal performance.

The core contribution is a Lagrangian framework that uses Finite-Time Lyapunov Exponent (FTLE) analysis, deformation-tensor methods and particle-trajectory tracking to identify and quantify the dynamically important saddle points in the wake. Their evolution correlates strongly with the time-dependent Nusselt number across geometries, which gives a physically interpretable predictor of heat-transfer behaviour. To support accurate simulation, I also developed a fourth-order accurate HOC–RK4 finite-difference solver that resolves vortices stably up to Re = 7500.

I wrote end-to-end simulation and post-processing pipelines in Python to extract flow features, analyse trajectories and turn large time-series datasets into quantitative insight. The work is under review at the International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer.

Overall, the research brings together numerical methods, scientific programming and data-driven analysis. Its applications include thermal management, flow optimisation and heat-transfer enhancement, and the same skills carry over to analytical and modelling problems in industry.
keywords: Computational Fluid Dynamics; Lagrangian Coherent Structures; Finite-Time Lyapunov Exponent; Unsteady Heat Transfer; Vortex Shedding; Bluff Body Flows; Particle Trajectory Tracking; High-Order Compact Schemes; Numerical Methods; Scientific Computing; Python; Data-Driven Analysis; Thermal Management

name: Praveen Kumar Reddy Annapureddy
thesis_title: SMD Solvent Descriptor Optimization and Thermodynamic Feasibility Assessment of Biomass-Derived Conversion Reactions in Supercritical Methanol and Ethanol
abstract: Supercritical fluids offer promising reaction environments for biomass conversion owing to their tunable physicochemical properties and enhanced solvent characteristics. Understanding solvent effects under supercritical conditions is essential for accurately predicting the thermodynamic feasibility of biomass-derived conversion reactions. The present study investigates the determination and optimization of Solvation Model based on Density (SMD) solvent descriptors for supercritical methanol and ethanol and evaluates the thermodynamic feasibility of biomass-derived molecular transformations using density functional theory (DFT). The SMD solvent descriptors are tuned to represent the distinctive physicochemical characteristics of supercritical solvents, incorporating temperature- and pressure-dependent fluid properties. The optimized descriptors are subsequently employed in implicit solvation calculations to investigate the influence of supercritical solvent environments on reaction energetics. DFT calculations are performed to determine the thermodynamic parameters, including enthalpy change (?H), Gibbs free energy change (?G), and electronic energy variations for selected biomass-derived conversion reactions. The results provide insights into the effects of solvent properties on reaction thermodynamics and identify energetically favourable and unfavourable conversion pathways. This integrated computational framework establishes a systematic approach for incorporating supercritical solvent effects into molecular-level thermodynamic investigations and contributes to a better understanding of biomass valorization in supercritical methanol and ethanol.
keywords: Supercritical Fluids; SMD Solvent Descriptors; Density Functional Theory (DFT); Implicit Solvation Model; Supercritical Methanol; Supercritical Ethanol; Thermodynamic Feasibility; Biomass Conversion

name: Prince Kumar Barnwal
thesis_title: Carbohydrates conversion to valuable chemicals: Advanced reactors, separation techniques and techno-economics
abstract: The conversion of renewable carbohydrates into valuable chemicals offers a pathway towards sustainable chemical manufacturing and reduced dependence on fossil resources. This thesis investigates integrated catalytic processes for producing platform chemicals, particularly 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF), levulinic acid, and furandicarboxylic acid, through advances in reactor engineering, product separation, and process evaluation. Reactive vacuum distillation is explored for efficient fructose dehydration to HMF, with emphasis on concentrated feeds, reaction kinetics, mechanistic understanding, and scalability. Organic acid catalysis in aqueous media is investigated for levulinic acid production, examining the effects of operating conditions, feed concentration, and reactor scale on product distribution and humin formation. Complementary studies address the catalytic oxidation of HMF to furandicarboxylic acid using engineered spinel oxide catalysts under aqueous conditions without added base. Downstream processing focuses on solvent extraction, adsorption, and vacuum distillation to recover target products and manage water, solvents, and reaction impurities. Experimental findings are integrated with process simulation to develop separation flowsheets and examine material and energy requirements. Technoeconomic evaluation provides a framework for assessing process feasibility and identifying opportunities for improvement. By connecting catalytic performance with reactor design, purification, and economic considerations, this research supports the development of scalable carbohydrate valorisation processes for future biorefineries and industrial applications.
keywords: Heterogeneous Catalysis; Advanced Reactors; Reactive Vacuum Distillation; Platform Chemicals; Separation Processes; AspenPlus Process Simulation; Technoeconomics; Biomass Valorisation

name: Priyanka Yadav
thesis_title: Post-Transcriptional Regulation of UPF3B by MicroRNA-874-3p During Neuroblastoma Cell Differentiation
abstract:
UPF3B is a core component of the nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD) pathway, and its
loss-of-function mutation causes intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, and childhood-onset schizophrenia. Although NMD and the microRNA (miRNA) pathway intersect at the 3’UTR, whether UPF3B loss reshapes the miRNA landscape, or whether UPF3B is itself regulated by a specific miRNA, remained unknown. Small RNA sequencing of UPF3B-knockout HEK293 cells identified 70 differentially expressed known miRNAs and 750 candidate novel miRNAs. Targets of the upregulated miRNAs were enriched for neurogenesis, axon guidance, and synaptic signalling. In silico prediction identified miR-874-
3p, upregulated upon UPF3B loss, as a candidate regulator of the UPF3B 3’UTR. Overexpression of miR-874-3p reduced UPF3B mRNA and protein by accelerating transcript
decay, and luciferase and mutagenesis assays confirmed direct, seed-dependent binding to the 3’UTR. This repression was sufficient to stabilise endogenous NMD substrates, an effect
reversed by an mIR-874-3p antagomir, indicating a negative feedback loop. During retinoic acid-induced differentiation of IMR32 and SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells, UPF3B declined as miR-874-3p increased, and miR-874-3p inhibition impaired expression of the neuronal marker NeuN. Differentiation was accompanied by reduced global NMD activity and suppressed TGF-?/BMP signalling, both of which were reversed by miR-874-3p inhibition. Thus, miR-874-3p regulates UPF3B post-transcriptionally, linking NMD attenuation to the TGF-? suppression during neuronal differentiation.
keywords: Nonsense-mediated mRNA decay;  UPF3B; MicroRNA; Regulation; Differentiation

name: Purushottam Kumar
thesis_title: Modelling, Degradation Analysis, and Hybridization of Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells for Vehicular Applications
abstract:
Proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) are promising for vehicles, but frequent load changes and start–stop operation accelerate degradation. Their slower transient response requires batteries to buffer power fluctuations and regenerative braking. This thesis investigates PEMFC modelling, degradation prognostics, and hybrid vehicle design and energy management.

A temperature-dependent, ten-parameter semi-empirical model is identified from polarization hysteresis data of two stacks. Reference-temperature centering and variable projection address parameter coupling, achieving median errors of 2.307 and 2.771 mV/cell. Hysteresis voltage gaps are 34 and 21 mV/cell. A double-layer capacitance, identified from 32 load-interruption events, represents transient voltage response.

Sequential parameter estimation is applied to IEEE PHM 2014 ageing datasets. A hybrid model combining the semi-empirical model and support vector regression predicts voltage with RMSEs of 0.00228 and 0.00330 V. An interface enables model comparison and prognostic visualization.

A temperature- and state-of-charge-dependent battery model is developed. Sizing analysis evaluates 1,125 configurations and selects 11 fuel-cell stacks with an 80S4P battery pack, satisfying end-of-life constraints. Health-adaptive energy management adjusts power sharing as fuel-cell capability declines. UDDS and US06 simulations show reduced peak fuel-cell current and cumulative current stress, with increased battery use. These findings support capability-aware modelling and energy management for PEMFC hybrid vehicles.
keywords: Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells; PEMFC Modelling; Parameter Estimation; Degradation Prognostics; Polarization Hysteresis; Lithium-Ion Batteries; Hybrid Electric Vehicles; Energy Management Strategy

name: Raagdeep Raj
thesis_title: Design and in-silico validation of multi-channel piezoelectric MEMS Sensor for Totally Implantable Cochlear Implant
abstract:
Totally Implantable Cochlear Implants (TICIs) aim to eliminate external sound-processing hardware while restoring auditory function through fully internalized sensing and stimulation. A critical challenge is developing miniaturized, low-power acoustic sensors capable of discriminating speech-relevant frequencies. This thesis investigates the design and in-silico verification of a multi-channel piezoelectric Microelectromechanical Systems (MEMS) sensor for internal acoustic sensing.

A biomimetic array of resonant piezoelectric cantilevers is developed to achieve frequency discrimination across the 200–8000 Hz auditory range. Channel distribution is guided by the anatomical frequency-position relationship. A hierarchical modelling framework integrating analytical formulations, coupled electromechanical Finite Element Models (FEM), and Reduced-Order Models (ROM) is established to evaluate mechanical resonance, electromechanical transduction, and electrical output characteristics. Parametric investigations examine the influence of structural geometry, multilayer configurations, and electrical boundary conditions on sensor performance. Particular emphasis is placed on frequency selectivity, sensitivity, inter-channel response, and model fidelity. The influence of middle-ear vibration transmission and mechanical coupling on sensor behaviour is also considered.

The research establishes a computational framework with engineering and anatomical requirement driven approach for systematic sensor design, performance optimization, and verification, supporting the development of miniaturized, energy-efficient acoustic sensing technologies for next-generation totally implantable cochlear implants.
keywords: MEMS Sensor; Acoustic and Vibration; in-silico validation; Auditory Implants;

name: RAHUL
thesis_title: Engineering V2Ox Thin Films for Single-Side Dopant-Free c-Si(n) Solar Cells: Optoelectronic Properties and Device Fabrication
abstract:
The growing demand for clean and sustainable energy has driven research into cost-effective and environmentally friendly silicon solar cells. Transition metal oxides (TMOs), particularly vanadium oxide (V2Ox), offer a promising dopant-free alternative to conventional amorphous silicon (a-Si:H) carrier-selective layers due to their high transparency, wide bandgap, and tuneable work function.
This thesis investigates the optimization of thermally evaporated V2Ox thin films as hole-selective layers for crystalline silicon (n-type) heterojunction solar cells. The effects of film thickness, substrate temperature, and post-deposition ultraviolet-ozone (UVO) treatment on the optical, chemical, morphological, and electronic properties of V2Ox are systematically studied. Additionally, indium tin oxide (ITO) films are optimized by varying RF power and argon flow rate to enhance their optoelectronic performance and transparency. Device simulations and electrical characterization are employed to understand interfacial properties, band alignment, and carrier selectivity.
Finally, single-sided dopant-free solar cells with the architecture Ag/ITO/V2Ox/c-Si(n)/Al are fabricated and systematically evaluated using optimized processing conditions. The devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 13.1%, the highest reported for single-sided V2Ox/c-Si(n)-based solar cells. These findings establish important correlations between thin-film properties, fabrication parameters, interfacial engineering, and device performance, highlighting the potential of V2Ox for simplified and cost-effective silicon photovoltaic technologies.
keywords: Silicon Heterojubction Solar Cells; Semiconductor Device Fabrication; Thin-Film Process Optimization; PECVD; Thermal Evaporation; RF-Sputtering; HWCVD; LPCVD; Dopant-Free Solar Cells; Transparent Conducting Oxides; Hole-Selective Contacts; UV-Ozone Surface Treatment; Optoelectronic Characterizations; FESEM; XPS; KPFM; Photo I-V; Solar Cells Device Simulations (AFORS-HET); Process Development and Optimization

name: RAHUL BHAGAWATI
thesis_title: A Multi-Stage Data-Driven Framework for Detection, Segmentation and Quantification of Hemoperitoneum in Trauma Patients Using Non-Contrast CT
abstract:
Hemoperitoneum indicates life-threatening internal bleeding following abdominal trauma that requires prompt identification. Although contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) is preferred, non-contrast CT (NCCT) is often used when contrast is contraindicated, unavailable, or impractical. Reliable assessment on NCCT is difficult because of overlapping Hounsfield Units, diffuse blood distribution, indistinct boundaries, and the predominance of non-hemorrhagic regions. Robust computational frameworks designed specifically for NCCT remain lacking.
This thesis addresses the gap through a staged investigation. First, a proof-of-concept evaluates CT-based segmentation under controlled conditions with known reference volumes. Second, classical image-processing algorithms, including the proposed Hounsfield Unit-based Volume quantification of Asymmetrical Objects (HUVAO), are tested on clinical NCCT data and shown to be limited by anatomical and imaging heterogeneity. Third, radiomics-driven explainable machine learning is developed for image-level detection, yielding the BoostFusion framework and Comprehensive Classification Score (CCS). Finally, patch-based deep learning explores patient-level localization, segmentation, and volumetric estimation, with uncertainty analysis and failure mode characterization. The Hemoperitoneum Burden Index (HBI) is proposed to stratify patients in terms of volumetric severity and spatial involvement.
Overall, the thesis demonstrates NCCT-based image-level detection and coarse spatial localization of hemoperitoneum, while identifying persistent segmentation challenges. It establishes a methodological foundation for further development and external validation.
keywords: Hemoperitoneum; Non-Contrast Computed Tomography; Medical Image Processing; Machine Learning; Deep Learning; Image Detection; Image Segmentation; Volumetric Quantification

name: Rajarshi Saha
thesis_title: Input Parallel Output Parallel Converters
abstract: Dual active bridge (DAB) is a  DC-DC converter. It provides galvanic isolation and bidirectional power flow. Dual phase-shift (DPS) modulation combines internal and external phase-shift in DAB. So, DPS provides 2 degree freedom of power flow. For a given power level, many combinations of phase-shift ratios are possible in DPS of DAB. In input parallel output parallel (IPOP) converter, multiple DABs are connected in input parallel output parallel mode. In IPOP, currents are distributed among all DABs and switching stress is reduced. So, in low voltage high power applications IPOP is suitable. In EV fast charging applications, high power is needed. So, IPOP is more advantageous than other DC-DC converters in EV application. Also high efficient power is needed in EV charging station. So, initially for each DAB using dual phase-shift (DPS) modulation at a given power level efficiency is optimized using Lagrange multiplier and the theoretical analysis is verified by  MATLAB simulation and experiments on laboratory prototype. Then in IPOP, efficiency is optimized at a given power level and it is verified in MATLAB simulink. In future the analysis is needed to be verified in hardware prototype.
keywords: Dual Active Bridge; Dual Phase-Shift; Efficiency Optimization; Input Parallel Output Parallel Converters

name: Rajeswari Suance P S
thesis_title: Reducing Communication Cost in Multi-Core Quantum Cores through Architecture and Compiler Co-Design
abstract: My research focuses on on-chip interconnects for classical and quantum processors. Multi-core quantum processors are a promising way to scale quantum computers. However, communication between cores through quantum teleportation introduces considerable delay and errors, making it a major bottleneck in system performance. My research minimizes this communication cost by optimizing the hardware architecture and the compiler. At the architectural level, we proposed a decentralized interconnect framework and teleportation strategies that reduce end-to-end communication latency by up to 40%. We also developed adaptive entanglement pre-generation policies that reduce teleportation latency. At the compiler level, we developed qubit mapping, layout synthesis, and scheduling techniques that account for network topology, link reliability, and congestion. On standard benchmarks, they reduce inter-core communication cost by more than 2×. We extended the SeQUeNCe quantum network simulator to model multi-core architectures and built quantum mapping framework using Qiskit and pytket. These works have been published at ACM Computing Frontiers, the IEEE Computer Society Annual Symposium on VLSI, and the IEEE International Conference on Quantum Communications, Networking, and Computing. I have prior experience in wireless network-on-chip and network-on-chip architectures for domain-specific accelerators. Beyond interconnects, I have a strong background in processor, GPU, cache, and DRAM memory.
keywords: Quantum Computer Architecture; Quantum Networks; Quantum Compilation; Network-on-Chip; Wireless Network-on-Chip; Hardware Accelerators; Cache Memory Management; GPU Architectures

name: Rakesh Panda
thesis_title: Design and Vibroacoustic Analysis of Sandwich Plates with Viscoelastic Composites and Piezoelectric Materials
abstract: Analytical and computational frameworks are developed to investigate the vibroacoustic behaviour of sandwich structures incorporating different reinforcement strategies. Initially, effective material properties of graphite-particle-reinforced viscoelastic composites are derived using differential-equation-based formulations. Subsequently, carbon-black nanoparticle-reinforced elastomers are characterised through master curves constructed from experimental data, with their frequency-dependent behaviour represented using a fractional-order derivative (FOD) model. The investigation is further extended to hybrid composites incorporating nanoparticle, fibre and metallic foil reinforcements. Different composite architectures are comparatively evaluated under equal-volume and equal-weight constraints in terms of effective material properties, structural dynamics and sound transmission loss. The influence of reinforcement configurations and weight constraints on vibroacoustic performance is examined, highlighting the benefits of hybrid reinforcement over conventional viscoelastic cores. Furthermore, fibre-reinforced hybrid composites are investigated with oblique fibre orientations in the transverse direction to tailor directional stiffness characteristics and improve vibration attenuation and sound transmission loss. The passive investigation is subsequently extended to active control of a plate–cavity system using piezoelectric patches. A modal-based control strategy incorporating automatic actuator-polarity switching is developed to simultaneously control structural and acoustic cavity modes, thereby enabling multimodal control and broadband noise isolation.
keywords: Finite Element Modelling; Multiphysics modelling; Active and Passive Noise Control; Numerical homogenization of Viscoelastic Composites; Fluid-structure interaction; Multimodal Vibration Control; Piezoelectric Actuation

name: Raktim Acharjee
thesis_title: Design and Implementation of Deep Learning Architectures for EEG-Based Emotion Recognition on Edge AI Platforms
abstract: EEG-based affective computing has significant potential for emotion recognition. However, signal artifacts, limited training data, demographic variability, and computational constraints pose significant challenges to its reliability and real-world deployment. This thesis systematically addresses these challenges through the development of robust, demographic-aware, and hardware-efficient deep learning frameworks. The research begins with developing deep learning-based denoising models for removing eyeblink, muscle, motion, and cardiac artifacts from EEG signals to improve signal quality. Subsequently, a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) based model is developed to generate synthetic EEG data, addressing data scarcity and improving model generalization. The research further investigates gender, age, and culture-related variability in EEG-based emotion recognition through deep learning, explainable AI, and functional connectivity analyses, revealing demographic differences in neural representations. These findings motivate the development of a demographic-aware deep learning framework aimed at improving recognition robustness, fairness, and generalizability across diverse populations. Finally, the research extends toward hardware-aware model optimization and FPGA deployment, incorporating quantization and resource-efficient inference strategies to enable real-time execution under hardware constraints. Overall, this thesis contributes toward developing reliable, interpretable, demographic-aware, and computationally efficient EEG-based affective computing systems for real-world applications.
keywords: Signal Processing; Biomedical Engineering; EEG; Machine Learning; Deep Learning; Artificial Intelligence (AI); Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCI); Emotion Recognition; Affective Computing; Explainable AI (XAI); Hardware Acceleration; Edge AI

name: Rama Karn
discipline: School of Interdisciplinary Studies and Sustainability
thesis_title: Design and Development of Heparin-Based Theragnostic Platforms for Bacterial Targeting, Imaging, and Antimicrobial Therapy
abstract: The growing global challenge of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) demands innovative molecular strategies that move beyond conventional antibiotics towards integrated bacterial detection and treatment. This thesis presents the design and evaluation of multifunctional molecular and heparin-based platforms that exploit fluorescence, supramolecular assembly and membrane-active chemistry for bacterial theragnostic applications. A metal-responsive heparin conjugate is developed by integrating a bacterial-targeting polymer with a fluorophore and amikacin, enabling bacteria-responsive fluorescence and localized antimicrobial functionality. Complementarily, an iridium-based molecular system is engineered to self-assemble into cationic nanoaggregates with potent antibacterial activity, while a heparin-functionalized analogue enables selective fluorescence imaging of bacteria in the presence of mammalian cells. The work further explores a heparin-conjugated cyclodextrin host–guest platform for the association and delivery of hydrophobic compounds and antibiotics. Incorporation of a tryptoline-based chloride-binding molecule introduces an antimicrobial-adjuvant strategy aimed at perturbing bacterial chloride homeostasis and enhancing antibiotic efficacy. Together, these studies address distinct barriers in infection management: selective bacterial visualization, direct antimicrobial action, and improved delivery and potentiation of existing drugs. By combining polymer targeting, metal-responsive fluorescence, organometallic self-assembly and ion-transport-related supramolecular chemistry, this research establishes complementary design principles for multifunctional antibacterial systems and advances the development of future targeted theragnostic approaches against drug-resistant bacterial infections.
keywords: Heparin-based biomaterials; Bacterial theragnostics; Supramolecular chemistry; Fluorescence imaging; Antimicrobial resistance

name: Ramanuj Shankar Pandey
discipline: School of Energy Science and Engineering
thesis_title: Energy recovery from waste shipping oil sludge via pyrolysis, co-pyrolysis and catalytic pyrolysis
abstract: This thesis investigates the recovery of energy and value-added products from waste shipping oil sludge through pyrolysis, co-pyrolysis with lignocellulosic biomass, and catalytic pyrolysis. Experiments were conducted in a fixed-bed reactor to evaluate the effects of temperature, feedstock composition, and catalyst properties on feedstock conversion and the distribution and composition of liquid, gaseous, and solid products. Shipping oil sludge was co-pyrolyzed with different biomass residues, including waste bamboo dust, while aluminosilicate-based and waste-derived materials were evaluated as catalysts. The products were characterized using GC, GC–MS, FTIR, NMR, elemental analysis, and other physicochemical techniques. Thermal degradation behavior, reaction kinetics, thermodynamic parameters, and probable reaction mechanisms were investigated using thermogravimetric analysis, model-free isoconversional methods, model-fitting approaches, and master-plot analysis. The findings demonstrate the potential of shipping oil sludge for producing hydrocarbon-rich pyrolysis oil and combustible gases, including hydrogen and light hydrocarbons. Co-pyrolysis and catalytic treatment influenced feedstock conversion and product distribution, while catalyst characteristics affected process performance. Overall, this research provides experimental and kinetic insights into the thermochemical valorization of shipping oil sludge and biomass residues for sustainable fuel and energy recovery.
keywords: Thermochemical Conversion; Pyrolysis; Co-pyrolysis; Catalytic Pyrolysis; Waste-to-Energy; Shipping Oil Sludge; Biomass Valorization; Reaction Kinetics; Thermodynamic Analysis; Catalyst Development; Fixed-Bed Reactor; Biofuels; Hydrogen Production; Hydrocarbon Recovery

name: RAMESH OJHA
thesis_title: On Some Numerical and Data-Driven Approach for Options Pricing
abstract: This research develops accurate and computationally efficient numerical methods for pricing European and American options under realistic volatility models. For European options, a fourth order collocation method provides accurate spatial approximations, while its spline representation facilitates calculation of option sensitivities, known as Greeks. For American options, a second order collocation framework incorporates early exercise constraints through a free boundary problem formulated as a variational inequality or linear complementarity problem. Ongoing empirical research collects, processes, and analyzes United States market option data across multiple underlying stocks, strike prices, and maturities. Numerical prices will be compared with market quotations and established benchmarks using suitable pricing error measures to evaluate accuracy and practical applicability. In parallel, neural network approaches are being developed to investigate further improvements in pricing accuracy and computational efficiency. Planned research includes high order finite element methods for European and American options under the Constant Elasticity of Variance model, emphasizing convergence, numerical stability, Greeks, and optimal exercise boundaries. Subsequent work will extend the framework to the Heston stochastic volatility model and associated higher dimensional pricing problems. Ultimately, the study aims to integrate rigorous numerical analysis with data driven learning for efficient option pricing, reliable sensitivity computation, and potential model calibration.
keywords: Option Pricing; Local Volatility; European and American Options; Collocation Method; Finite Element Method; CEV Model; Heston Model; Machine Learning; Financial Market Data.

name: Ravi Prakash
thesis_title: Investigations of Advanced Electrochemical Post-Processing Techniques for Metal Additive Manufacturing Components: An Experimental and Numerical Approach
abstract: Metal additive manufacturing makes complex components possible, yet rough as-built surfaces can limit fatigue performance and biocompatibility. This work combines numerical modeling and experiments to improve electropolishing (EP) and plasma electrochemical polishing (PEP) of complex components, including dental implants. COMSOL models examine interfacial transport and thermal behavior, while experimental work covers setup development, statistical parameter optimization, and surface characterization. EP simulations show how concentration differences within the viscous film influence material removal at surface peaks and valleys. For PEP, polishing depends on vapor gas envelope thickness, while applied potential and surface roughness strongly affect its thermal behavior. Under optimized conditions, dual-stage electropolishing (DSEP) achieves a 21% improvement over conventional EP. Polishing times in both stages emerge as the most significant parameters. The PEP setup uses a dynamic electrolyte system to maintain stable plasma discharge during extended polishing. DSEP yields more uniform surface morphology, whereas PEP produces a more reflective finish through localized polishing. Both treatments improve the corrosion resistance of additively manufactured 316L stainless steel. These results guide process selection based on the required surface uniformity and finish. Ongoing work explores high-speed imaging and speckle metrology to study interfacial phenomena, monitor roughness changes, and establish feedback for identifying polishing completion.
keywords: Metal Additive Manufacturing; Electropolishing; Plasma Electrochemical Polishing; Numerical Modeling; Process Optimization; Surface Characterization

name: Rishabh Mahanta
thesis_title: Efficient Management of Intermittently Powered systems for forward progress of applications
abstract:
Intermittent computing systems (ImC) are a product of evolving edge devices. ImC is envisioned as a possible substitute for devices with consistent power and battery backup. The need for creative architectural designs has resulted from the difficulties of unreliable power-supply, which causes frequent interruptions in task execution, prevent the widespread deployment of such systems. 

Our work proposes newer architectures for ImC that uses a volatile SRAM cache to minimize runtime interruptions and speed up task execution. There are speed and energy benefits to faster writing to SRAM caches. Frequently written blocks are stored on a tiny STT scratchpad memory in case of evictions. 
   
However, as these systems lack active cooling mechanisms, elevated on-chip temperatures lead to significant leakage in volatile components such as SRAM caches, resulting in severe energy loss and reduced reliability, especially in environments where the power supply is constant and the ambient temperature is high. We design a temperature-aware and energy-efficient architecture for ImC systems that dynamically mitigates thermal-induced leakage. Implemented on the GEM5 simulator and analyzed using McPAT, NVSim, CACTI, and HotSpot. The results demonstrate that incorporating thermal awareness into the architectural design of ImC systems is essential for achieving energy efficiency and long-term reliability.
keywords: computer architecture;microarchitecture;embedded systems;edge computing;intermittent computing;model inference;artificial intelligence

name: Riyaj Uddin Khan
thesis_title: Design and Development of Hardware-Efficient Learning Architectures for EEG-Based Epileptic Seizure Detection on FPGA Platforms
abstract:
My research focuses on energy-efficient digital hardware, FPGA acceleration, and machine learning for biomedical signal processing, with particular emphasis on EEG-based epileptic seizure detection. As a PhD researcher in Electronics and Electrical Engineering at IIT Guwahati, I investigate algorithm–hardware co-design, connecting mathematical optimization and neural network architecture to practical hardware constraints.

My doctoral work spans three complementary systems. The first implements a fixed-point Twin Support Vector Machine with sequential minimal optimization on a Virtex-7 FPGA, emphasizing compact arithmetic and resource-efficient classification. The second, HD²-Net, combines hierarchical feature extraction, grouped dilated convolutions, and contextual pooling, achieving a reported accuracy of 99.25% on CHB-MIT with INT8 inference on a ZCU102. The third, CF-ResNet, explores local–global feature fusion and residual synchronization, with 10.314 million multiply–accumulate operations and a reported FPGA inference latency of 4.23 ms.

Across these projects, I evaluate classification performance, hardware resources, latency, memory requirements, and estimated power consumption. My technical experience includes MATLAB, HDL Coder, Verilog, Vivado, fixed-point design, hardware verification, and performance analysis. I also bring teaching-assistance experience in Verilog-based system design and analog integrated circuits. I seek academic roles involving teaching and collaborative research, as well as industry positions in RTL design, FPGA engineering, embedded AI, and digital hardware optimization.
keywords: FPGA-Based Hardware Acceleration; VLSI Design; RTL Design and Verification; Digital System Design; Algorithm–Hardware Co-Design; Embedded Artificial Intelligence; Deep Learning Accelerators; Biomedical Signal Processing; EEG-Based Epileptic Seizure Detection; Low-Power and High-Performance Computing

name: ROHIT KUMAR
discipline: School of Interdisciplinary Studies and Sustainability
thesis_title: Ph. D. Thesis: Vehicular count-based prediction and forecasting of Particulate Matter, Gaseous-pollutant, and AQI in the  Guwahati City with Machine Learning and Deep Learning models
abstract:
The research develops a cost-effective, data-driven framework for predicting and forecasting urban air quality by integrating vehicular activity, meteorological parameters, and air-quality observations using Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) techniques. The study focuses on Guwahati, India, using 1,776 daily observations (2019–2023) obtained from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) and Assam State Transport Corporation (ASTC). Five major air-quality indicators namely, PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NO2, O3 and the Air Quality Index (AQI) were investigated using multiple ML and DL algorithms. Feature engineering, including lag variables, rolling statistics and seasonal decomposition, alongside cross-validation and hyperparameter optimization, was employed to improve predictive performance and model generalization.
Among the evaluated models, XGBoost consistently demonstrated superior predictive performance for particulate matter, gaseous pollutants and AQI, while Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) emerged as the most effective DL architecture, particularly for PM2.5 and PM10. Correlation analysis further identified strong associations of AQI with PM2.5 (0.92) and PM10 (0.89). The findings establish the potential of integrating vehicular-count data with meteorological and temporal features for urban air-quality assessment. The proposed framework offers practical applications in environmental monitoring, pollution management, public-health risk assessment and sustainable urban planning, particularly in rapidly developing cities with limited monitoring resources.
keywords: Air Pollution assessment; Machine learning; Deep learning, Real-time monitoring

name: Roopjyoti Misra
thesis_title: Stimuli-responsive Turn-on Fluorogenic Prodrugs of Selected Inhibitors Targeting Aldose Reductase and Cyclooxygenase-2 towards the Effective Treatment of Cancer.
abstract: I am a final year PhD candidate in Chemistry at IIT Guwahati, working at the interface of organic synthesis, medicinal chemistry and chemical biology. My research focuses on designing and synthesizing stimuli-responsive, fluorescence-based prodrugs for targeted cancer therapy, and evaluating their activity through spectroscopic and biological assays. I have authored six peer-reviewed publications, including two in the prestigious Journal of Medicinal Chemistry and contributed to a patent application. I bring hands-on experience in multi-step synthesis, chromatographic purification and analytical techniques including NMR, HPLC, mass spectrometry, UV-Vis and fluorescence spectroscopy, along with proficiency in ChemDraw, MestreNova and Origin. As an experienced student operator for Bruker NMR spectrometers, I have independently supported research groups across the department. I have also served as a teaching assistant for undergraduate and postgraduate laboratory courses and mentored three MSc thesis students. I am analytical, detail-oriented and collaborative, with strong communication skills built through teaching, conference presentations and event coordination. I am keen to apply my scientific training and problem-solving abilities in a role that values research, innovation and continuous learning.
keywords: Medicinal Chemistry; Multi-step Organic Synthesis; Targeted Drug Delivery; Cancer Therapeutics; Anticancer Agents; Drug Discovery; Column and Flash Chromatography; NMR Spectroscopy; HPLC; Mass Spectrometry; UV-Visible Spectroscopy; Fluorescence Spectroscopy; FT-IR Spectroscopy; Bruker NMR Operation; Scientific Writing; Teaching and Mentoring; Good Laboratory Practices.

name: Rushabh Kamalakar Kale
thesis_title: Experimental and simulation studies on AEM electrolyzer for green H2 production and utilization.
abstract:
The increasing demand for clean and sustainable energy has intensified research into green hydrogen production. AEMWE has emerged as a promising technology because it can potentially combine the advantages of alkaline electrolysis with the use of relatively low-cost electrocatalysts.
Therefore, this research is focus on developing a tailored electrolyte additives using ionic liquid for enhanced hydrogen evolution reaction in AEMWE. The tailored electrolytes are synthesized based on the quantum chemical calculations using Conductor-like Screening Model-segment Activity Coefficient (COSMO-SAC) approach. The synthesized electrolytes are analysed using various electrochemical techniques such as LSV, Tafel analysis, CA, and EIS, for the performance evaluation. Further, optimized electrolyte is tested in AEMWE for hydrogen production efficiency analysis. 
Using the performance parameters from the tested electrolytes on AEMWE, the process simulation software is used to develop a large scale plant for hydrogen production and utilization to produce power from AEMFC and STU. However, to showcase the utilization of produced green hydrogen for value added chemical is done by producing green ammonia. Here, new approach was adopted for green ammonia production using industrial waste-water. By integrating electrolyte development, electrochemical understanding, and process-level assessment, this research aimed to bridge the gap between fundamental HER studies and scalable AEMWE.
keywords: Anion exchange membrane, Water electrolyzer, Electrochemical cell, Green hydrogen production, Green ammonia production, Hydrogen evolution reaction, Aspen Plus, DFT, Fuel cell, Steam turbine unit, Ion exchange column

name: Sachin Sahu
thesis_title: Intelligent Reflecting Surface-Assisted UAV Networks: Optimization and Learning for Coverage, Energy and Security.
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRSs) are promising technologies for next-generation wireless networks: UAVs extend coverage flexibly, while IRSs reshape the radio environment at low cost. Designing them together, however, leads to non-convex and often NP-hard optimization problems, made harder by imperfect channel information, hardware impairments and jamming. This thesis develops optimization- and learning-based solutions for IRS-assisted UAV networks in three settings. First, it combines satellites, UAVs and STAR-IRSs to connect users in rural and hilly regions, using a genetic algorithm for UAV trajectories and a closed-form phase-shift design to improve both fairness and overall data rate. Second, it proposes an energy-efficient UAV-IRS framework that wirelessly powers edge devices running multiple federated learning services, minimizing energy use with a continuous genetic algorithm and a greedy auction approach. Third, it protects users of a rate-splitting multi-UAV network from a jammer of unknown position and power, pairing model-based precoding and IRS design with a deep reinforcement learning agent that repositions the UAVs. Together, these results show how mathematical optimization and machine learning can make UAV networks fairer, more energy-efficient and more resilient.
keywords: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs); intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS);rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA); anti-jamming; genetic algorithm; deep reinforcement learning(DRL) STAR-IRS; satellite communication;

name: Saptarshi Samanta
thesis_title: Linking haptic modalities, game events  and player traits
abstract: Haptic feedback, the vibrations and forces players feel through a game controller, is now standard on modern consoles. Yet game designers have little systematic guidance on which game events should trigger it and how strong it should feel. My doctoral research at IIT Guwahati addresses this gap through haptic experience design for entertainment digital games. A bibliometric study first showed that entertainment games remain underrepresented in haptics research. Building on this, I developed the Game Event Model (GEM). It sorts game events into two types: those triggered by a player’s action and those triggered by the player’s location. I validated it through playtests and directed content analysis of about 750 event types across eight games, with inter-rater reliability checks. A second experiment with 49 participants in a custom Unreal Engine 5 environment linked how strong players felt vibrations to be (Soft, Medium, Harsh) to accelerometer measurements, establishing a perception-grounded vibration scale. A third study examined whether player traits shape haptic preferences and found no significant effect. This suggests designers can calibrate haptics around game events rather than player types. Together, the work gives designers a structured, evidence-based toolkit for deciding where and how to use haptic feedback in games.
keywords: HCI; Haptic experience design; Games User Research; Game Design; User Experience Design

name: Sarbani mandal
thesis_title: Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy for Electric Vehicle Batteries: Circuit Design and Analysis
abstract: Accurate characterization and modeling of lithium-ion batteries are essential for understanding their electrochemical behavior, assessing degradation, and ensuring reliable operation in electric vehicle applications. This research presents an integrated framework combining electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), equivalent circuit modeling (ECM), and data-driven analysis for battery characterization and performance evaluation. A dedicated impedance measurement system is designed, prototyped, and experimentally validated to characterize lithium-ion cells under varying operating conditions. The measured impedance responses are analyzed using equivalent circuit models to estimate electrochemical parameters and investigate their dependence on temperature, state of charge, and degradation. Statistical analysis and unsupervised machine learning techniques are employed to explore relationships between impedance characteristics and battery operating conditions, supporting impedance-based diagnostics. Furthermore, the relationship between impedance characteristics and irreversible heat generation is investigated to assess battery temperature rise under different operating conditions. The study also extends from cell-level characterization to battery pack modeling, examining the influence of cell-to-cell impedance variations on pack performance and output energy. By integrating experimental measurements, electrochemical modeling, and data-driven approaches, this research provides a comprehensive methodology for investigating battery behavior across cell and pack levels, with potential applications in battery diagnostics, thermal assessment, and performance optimization for electric mobility.
keywords: Advance battery characterization

name: Satish Kumar
thesis_title: Advanced Functionalized Electrode Materials for  Desalination and Selective Resource Recovery by Capacitive  Deionization
abstract:
My doctoral research focuses on developing advanced nanostructured porous electrode materials and electrochemical technologies for sustainable water treatment and selective resource recovery. I have synthesized and engineered various carbon-based nanomaterials, graphene derivatives, metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), and hybrid nanocomposites through electrode modification, surface functionalization, and incorporation of redox-active components. These approaches enhance interfacial charge transfer, Faradaic redox reactions, ion-selective electrosorption, electrochemical performance, and electrode stability.
My research integrates capacitive deionization, redox-assisted electrochemical separation, and electrocoagulation for brackish water desalination, hardness removal, wastewater treatment, and selective recovery of valuable metals, including lithium, nickel, and copper, from complex industrial streams and spent battery leachates.
Building on this expertise, my future research aims to develop multifunctional electrode materials for critical mineral and rare-earth element recovery from secondary resources, including spent batteries, electronic waste, and industrial residues. I also envision extending these engineered nanomaterials and redox-active electrodes toward advanced battery technologies, electrochemical energy storage, and CO? capture and conversion. My overarching objective is to integrate materials innovation, electrochemical process development, and resource circularity to deliver scalable technologies for environmental sustainability and clean energy.
keywords: Electrochemistry, Electrode Engineering, Critical minerals, Resource recovery,  Desalination

name: Satyendra Verma
thesis_title: Design and Development of sulfonamide-Functionalized  Molecular and Coordination Materials for Chemical Sensing, Molecular Recognition and Adsorption.
abstract: This research explores the principles of supramolecular chemistry and crystal engineering to understand how microscopic molecular self-assembly dictates macroscopic material properties. Early investigations focused on designing zinc- and cobalt-based coordination polymers using dicarboxylate linkers and flexible urea-imidazole ligands, demonstrating precise control over supramolecular architecture and dimensionality for applications such as DNA interactions and dye adsorption. Subsequent work expanded into organic molecular crystals, utilizing Schiff-base conjugates of sulfa drugs and 2-hydroxynaphthalene-based imines to investigate the intricate interplay between hydrogen bonding, optical behaviour, and tautomerism through combined experimental crystallography and theoretical calculations. Building upon these pharmaceutical building blocks, recent efforts have advanced into molecular sensing, successfully developing fluorescent probes for the selective recognition of biological targets like erythromycin. Furthermore, investigations into crystal packing and polymorphism—highlighted by the isolation of a novel third polymorph of N-amino-1,8-naphthalimide—underscore how subtle variations in crystallization conditions govern intermolecular interactions and solid-state architecture.
keywords: Supramolecular Chemistry;  Crystal Engineering;  Coordination Polymers; Adsorption; Cocrystals;  polymorph; Tautomerism & Hydrogen Bonding;  Molecular Sensing / Fluorescent Probes;

name: Sauradeep Bhattacharjee
thesis_title: Extraction in Liquid–Liquid Systems in the Presence of Interfacial Instability: Experimental Studies, Mathematical Modelling, Simulation using GROMACS, and Data Correlation using Machine Learning
abstract: This research investigates enhanced solute transfer in various stirred liquid–liquid ternary systems under energy-driven interfacial instability. The study examines phenomena occurring during mass transfer when the interface experiences primarily energy-driven and, secondarily, Marangoni and Rayleigh–Taylor instabilities. Systems were selected to cover both the aqueous-to-organic and reverse-transfer directions. Static experiments identified the onset and sustained-instability concentrations, the latter being used in stirred LLE experiments. Solute concentrations were measured at three spatial locations in each phase: bulk, interfacial center, and interfacial edge. Two stirring speeds (100 and 200 RPM) were used in one system for each transfer direction. Interfacial tension–concentration relationships and distribution coefficients were also determined for each system. Based on experimental observations, the mathematical criterion for energy-driven interfacial instability proposed in previous studies was reinterpreted in light of the thermodynamic aspects of molecular energy. This reinterpretation was validated through molecular dynamics simulations using GROMACS. Generalized mass transfer coefficient correlations for the raffinate and extract phases and the interface were developed using mathematical modelling and solving systems of nonlinear equations, respectively. Machine learning was subsequently employed on the mathematical models to improve correlation accuracy.
keywords: Liquid-Liquid Extraction; Interfacial Instability; Molecular Dynamics Simulation; Mathematical Modelling; Physics-Informed Machine Learning

name: Sauranga Das
thesis_title: Manual lifting of passenger car (heavy load) with mechanical device: user  centered design approach
abstract: Urban flash floods strand vehicles and endanger occupants, yet suitable rescue equipment remains scarce. This study presents the design, structural-dynamic assessment, and ergonomic evaluation of a manually operated tubular steel vehicle lifting device for flood emergency applications. A finite element model was developed in ANSYS to evaluate structural integrity under loaded conditions. Because floodwater flow imposes stochastic excitation, modal characterization was combined with flow-induced random vibration analysis using power spectral density (PSD) inputs. Response metrics, including displacement and stress, were extracted to identify critical frequency ranges. The results reveal critical resonance risks under loaded conditions, where natural frequencies may coincide with dominant excitation content and amplify response. Findings guide design refinement to shift resonant modes away from excitation bands.As the device is manually operated, ergonomics is equally critical. Three handle designs were ergonomically evaluated through digital human modeling in CATIA V5, including biomechanical and vision analyses, and through physical Rapid Entire Body Assessment (REBA) based on observed joint angles of users operating a hydraulic pump fitted with each design. Handle B emerged as the best design. The complete assembly was also assessed for operator interaction during deployment and lifting. Together, the results support safe, user-friendly flood-rescue design.
keywords: Mechanical Design, Finite Element Method, Ergonomics, Human Factor, Digital Human Modelling

name: Sayan Haldar
thesis_title: A Machine Learning Framework for Projecting Groundwater Level and Quality Risk in West Bengal, India, under CMIP6 Climate Scenarios
abstract: Groundwater resources in West Bengal, India, face mounting stress from climate change, intensive abstraction and both geogenic and anthropogenic contamination. Yet district-scale assessments that integrate future groundwater quantity and quality remain limited. So, a machine learning framework is developed to project groundwater level and quality risk across all 23 districts of West Bengal under four CMIP6 Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0 and SSP5-8.5) through 2100. District-scale rainfall and temperature projections are derived from 16 CMIP6 models, using an ensemble selected for model performance and independence and bias-corrected by quantile delta mapping. These projections drive machine learning models of groundwater level. From these models, a composite Groundwater Vulnerability Index (GVI) and a Time-of-Divergence (ToD) metric identify where and when aquifers depart from historical conditions. Groundwater quality observations (2016–2022) are then integrated to evaluate quality vulnerability, risk and susceptibility under projected conditions. The combined quantity and quality outputs provide a decision-support basis for managed aquifer recharge (MAR): prioritizing recharge zones, timing interventions ahead of projected divergence, and excluding sites susceptible to contaminant mobilization. The framework therefore enables policymakers to plan and manage aquifers within administrative boundaries, supporting climate-adaptive groundwater governance.
keywords: CMIP6; Shared Socioeconomic Pathways(SSPs); Machine Learning (ML); Groundwater Vulnerability; Groundwater Quality Risk; Managed Aquifer Recharge (MAR); Groundwater governance; West Bengal

name: Shaktimaan Debendra Pratap
thesis_title: Multiple Access Techniques for Next-Gen Wireless Applications: Performance Analysis and Optimization
abstract: My research focuses on the design, performance analysis, and optimization of next-generation wireless communication and Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) systems, particularly involving Rate-Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA), Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA), and Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces (IRS). I investigate uplink and downlink communication performance, achievable and ergodic rates, outage probability, and sensing performance under practical operating conditions, considering imperfect channel state information, imperfect successive interference cancellation, residual hardware impairments, and diverse fading environments. My work combines stochastic channel modeling, analytical derivations using moment-generating functions, probability distributions, special mathematical functions, and numerical integration techniques, along with extensive Monte Carlo simulations. I also formulate and solve non-convex resource-allocation problems involving transmit power, power allocation, common-rate distribution, and sensing constraints using optimization frameworks such as successive convex approximation and majorization-minimization. The overarching objective is to develop tractable analytical models and efficient optimization strategies for reliable, spectrum-efficient, and sensing-aware 6G wireless networks. These contributions can help industries design and optimize advanced wireless infrastructure for connected vehicles, industrial IoT, smart cities, and future intelligent communication systems.
keywords: Wireless Communication; Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC); Non-Orthogonal & Rate-Splitting Multiple Access (NOMA & RSMA); Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces (IRS); Optimization Techniques; Beamforming

name: Shamim Hossain Shah
thesis_title: Interfacial Engineering of Nanoscale Matter for Enhanced Energy and Electron Transport and Light-Matter Interactions
abstract: Interfacial engineering of nanomaterials offers opportunities to control charge and energy transfer processes and light-matter interactions for applications in energy conversion and molecular sensing. This thesis investigates two approaches: controlling interfacial photophysics in lead halide perovskite/quantum dot hybrids and functional chemical engineering of MoS2 moiré superlattices. In perovskite/CuInS2 hybrid nanoarchitectures, halide-dependent band alignment was found to govern the competition between energy and electron transfer. Furthermore, surface functionalization of CsPbBr3 with 4-aminothiophenol enabled rapid hole extraction in CsPbBr3/AgInS2 hybrids, generating trion states that facilitated efficient sequential electron transfer and enhanced photocurrent. The second part explores boron doping and molecular functionalization of MoS2 moiré superlattices. Controlled boron doping improved hydrogen evolution reaction activity, with an optimal doping condition yielding the lowest overpotential, attributed to modified charge distribution and interlayer coupling. Additionally, 4-aminothiophenol functionalization enabled control over interlayer twist-angle distributions, thereby yielding surface-enhanced Raman scattering through enhanced charge transfer. Collectively, these findings establish strategies for composition and surface engineering to tailor interfacial charge dynamics and light-matter interactions, highlighting the potential of hybrid nanostructures and moiré quantum materials for energy conversion and ultrasensitive molecular detection.

name: shamshad alam
thesis_title: Design and Optimization of Resonator- and Nanocavity-Based Optical Refractive Index Sensors on SOI Platform with Machine Learning Assistance
abstract: I am a silicon photonics engineer completing my Ph.D. in Electronics and Electrical Engineering at the Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati, with over five years of hands-on experience in designing, simulating and optimizing photonic devices on the silicon-on-insulator platform. My doctoral research focuses on compact, high-performance refractive index sensors based on ring and racetrack resonators and two-dimensional photonic crystal nanocavities, applied to detecting dengue, tuberculosis, waterborne pathogens, milk adulteration and blood viscosity. I use the Ansys Lumerical suite (FDTD, MODE and INTERCONNECT) for device and circuit simulation, KLayout for GDS layout, and Python for automation, data analysis and machine-learning surrogate models that speed up inverse design. Before my Ph.D., I completed an M.Tech. in VLSI Design at NIT Jalandhar, where I modelled nanowire FET biosensors in Silvaco TCAD and worked with Cadence Virtuoso. I have cleanroom training in UV photolithography and nanofabrication from IISc Bangalore and IIT Guwahati. My work has produced six journal papers, twelve conference papers and four book chapters. As Chairperson of the IEEE Student Branch at IIT Guwahati, I led technical teams and events. I am seeking an industry role in photonic integrated circuit design.

name: Sharmistha Masih
thesis_title: Decision Support System for Sustainable Construction
abstract: Modern construction projects demand high performance across conflicting objectives, including time, cost, quality, environmental sustainability and social sustainability. However, optimising these facets in constrained environments with multiple execution alternatives remains a critical challenge. Existing frameworks often lack scalability, overlook sustainability, and fail to integrate productivity metrics for multimodal activities in time, cost and resource-constrained environment. To bridge the gap, this research develops a comprehensive Decision Support System (DSS) driven by a novel activity-subactivity decomposition strategy. The framework utilises a nested optimisation model, combining state-of-the-art exact and metaheuristic optimization algorithms. Furthermore, sustainability metrics are evaluated through an enhanced FAHP-TOPSIS framework. By integrating machine learning-based algorithms, the proposed approach uniquely preserves the diverse expert perspectives inherent in sustainability assessments. Validation through a real-world case study yielded crucial industry insights: sustainability do not inherently increase with project cost, but rather hinge on strategic activity-mode selection. Moreover, the study reveals a synergy between cost and sustainability in low labour-cost economies like India, whereas quality and sustainability exhibit a strong negative correlation. Ultimately, this thesis delivers a highly scalable, implementable DSS that empowers decision-makers and construction practitioners to quantitatively integrate sustainability goals into the early phases of construction planning, significantly enhancing overall project performance.
keywords: Construction Management; Operations Research; Mathematical Optimization; Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM); Decision Analysis; Tradeoff; Sustainability; AI/ML in construction; Construction Planning; Scheduling; Decision Support; Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling Problem (RCPSP)

name: SHASHI BHUSHAN SINGH
thesis_title: Structure-Property-Performance Relationships in Engineered Cerium-Based Metal-Organic Framework for Heavy Metals Remediation
abstract: The research investigates the rational design and engineering of cerium-based metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) for the remediation of heavy-metal-contaminated aqueous environments. MOF-808(Ce) was systematically modified through post-synthetic ligand functionalization using nitrogen-, oxygen-, and sulfur-containing functionalities, metal-node engineering through Ce/Mo bimetallic integration, and composite fabrication with zeolite. The developed adsorbents were evaluated for adsorption performance, metal-ion selectivity, competitive adsorption, regeneration, and applicability in different water matrices. Comprehensive investigations of adsorption kinetics, equilibrium isotherms, and thermodynamics were undertaken to elucidate adsorption behaviour and underlying structure–property relationships. Response surface methodology (RSM) was employed for process optimization, while density functional theory (DFT) was incorporated to investigate molecular-level interactions and adsorption mechanisms. Artificial neural network (ANN) modelling was explored for predictive analysis of adsorption performance. Furthermore, MOF–zeolite composites were immobilized in alginate matrices and evaluated under continuous-flow fixed-bed column conditions using established breakthrough models. Spectroscopic and physicochemical characterization provided insights into metal coordination, surface complexation, and ion-exchange mechanisms. Overall, this work integrates functional material synthesis, computational chemistry, statistical optimization, machine-learning-based prediction, and adsorption process engineering to advance multifunctional MOF-based materials for sustainable water treatment.
